tools.name: register_agent
tools.description: Create an agent identity bound to a principal, with a spending mandate (limits in minor units). Returns agent_key once; send it on every later call. The first agent of a new principal_id also receives principal_key (once): the principal owns the wallet, and every later register_agent for that princi

tools.name: rotate_principal_key
tools.description: Replace your principal's principal_key. Needs your agent credentials and the current principal_key (argument or X-Principal-Key header). Returns the new key once; the old one stops working. Existing agents are unaffected. A principal registered before keys existed has none: any of its agents can cal

tools.name: get_policies
tools.description: Returns every policy as machine-readable JSON (mandate, refund, dispute, supplier trust, registration), the store terms and the product/agent JSON Schemas, so you can reason about terms before buying.

tools.name: search_plans
tools.description: Search eSIM data plans from trusted suppliers. Filter by destination country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or region, minimum data, validity and price. Results are sorted by final price unless sort says otherwise. Suppliers below the trust threshold are excluded and listed in excluded_suppliers.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Lock the final price for one product for a short time (quote_ttl_seconds in store terms). Also returns a mandate pre-check and the refund terms, so you know before buying whether the purchase will be allowed.

tools.name: purchase
tools.description: Buy the product in a quote. Enforces the mandate and the wallet policy, holds the amount in the principal's wallet, orders from the supplier, debits the wallet, and returns the order with the eSIM delivery payload and a signed receipt. If the wallet is short, fails with WALLET_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS and

tools.name: get_wallet
tools.description: Balance, available funds (balance minus pending holds), open top-up links, recent top-ups and recent ledger entries of the wallet of the principal you act for. Shared by all of the principal's agents. Amounts in minor units.

tools.name: get_topup_link
tools.description: Create a hosted payment URL to hand to your human principal. They pay in ILS on the acquirer's page (PayPlus); you never see card data. amount_minor is in `currency`: USD (the wallet credit you want; the ILS charge is computed at today's rate) or ILS (the exact charge). The wallet is credited in USD

tools.name: order_status
tools.description: Current order state, eSIM delivery payload, activation and data usage from the supplier, receipts and disputes.

tools.name: regenerate_activation
tools.description: For one of your own delivered orders whose activation code (QR / LPA) does not install: asks the supplier for a fresh code and returns the new delivery payload. The previous code may stop working. Not every supplier supports it (NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_SUPPLIER); then open a dispute with reason not_working

tools.name: request_refund
tools.description: Reasons "unused" and "changed_plans" are voluntary refunds under the refund policy. Reasons "not_delivered", "not_working" and "duplicate_purchase" open a dispute under the dispute policy, which can refund fully, partially, reject, or escalate to a human. A dispute about a delivered eSIM is credited

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Check a receipt's signature and that it matches its hash-chained ledger entry.

tools.name: sandbox_simulate_topup_payment
tools.description: Sandbox only. Acts as the principal paying a get_topup_link URL: the mock provider sends a PayPlus-format IPN through the same webhook path production uses, and the wallet is credited. outcome "declined" simulates a failed card.

tools.name: sandbox_simulate_activation
tools.description: Sandbox only. Marks the order's eSIM as installed and used, as if the traveler activated it. Use it to exercise refund and dispute rules.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "rotate_principal_key" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_topup_link · Private data: register_agent, rotate_principal_key, purchase, get_wallet, get_topup_link, sandbox_simulate_topup_payment · Public sink: register_agent, sandbox_simulate_topup_payment · Destructive: sandbox_simulate_topup_payment.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_topup_link · Private data: register_agent, rotate_principal_key, purchase, get_wallet, get_topup_link, sandbox_simulate_topup_payment · Public sink: register_agent, sandbox_simulate_topup_payment · Destructive: sandbox_simulate_topup_payment

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "purchase" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
